label: <DEL> step, boosted by last token z/e/b/0 or first token u/p/o/a/2
predicate: (phase == 1) & (isin(prev_tok, [tok("z"), tok("e"), tok("b"), 26]) | isin(first_tok, [tok("u"), tok("p"), tok("o"), tok("a"), 28]))
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step: 83% of activation mass and 81% of active steps are at <DEL>, and it never fires in the copy phase. Only about 11% of <DEL> steps are active, though. Which ones depends on the sequence contents. It is more likely when the last original token (prev_tok) is z, e, b or 0 (3-6x lift) and when the first original token is u, p, o, a or 2 (2-4x lift). It is also more likely for mid-length sequences (L=4-6) than for L=8-9. The other ~17% of mass is in the original phase, mostly on input z (4.8% rate there) and a little on b, and never at t=0 or t=1. Adding the z clause raises recall to 0.96 but drops precision. The predicate reaches only F1 ~0.38 on dev (mass recall 0.68). The rest of the <DEL> selectivity looks like a graded function of the full prefix that no simple token rule captures. Magnitude is small (max 0.063) and largest at <DEL> after z/e-ending sequences or u/p-starting ones.
